codes.meaning: The property exists and its type is not one a literal can be written into: a struct without a text form the writer knows, an array, a map, a delegate.
codes.fix: Leave the property out of the call and set it on the asset by hand, or ask for the type to be supported; the message names the property and its class.

codes.title: Invalid reflected property target.
codes.meaning: A literal was to be written into a null object or property. Internal error.
codes.fix: Report it with the source.

codes.title: '{0}' is set twice by '#pragma material'; it was already set on line {1}.
codes.meaning: One `#pragma material` key is set twice, possibly on two different lines — the lines are merged into one settings table. Keys are compared without regard to case, as the 1.x settings were.
codes.fix: Delete one of the two. The message names the line the first one was written on.

codes.title: 'Backend' has no value; write 'Backend = Graph' or 'Backend = ThinCustom'. An empty value meant Graph in 1.x and means nothing now.
codes.meaning: `Backend` was given an empty value. 1.x read `Backend = ""` as `Graph`, which silently overrode the project default with a value nobody wrote; 2.0 refuses it rather than carry the trap forward.
codes.fix: Write `Backend = Graph` or `Backend = ThinCustom`, or delete the key to take the project default.

codes.title: 'Backend = {0}' is not a backend; the backends are 'Graph' and 'ThinCustom'.
codes.meaning: `Backend` names something that is not a backend.
codes.fix: The backends are `Graph` (a visible material graph) and `ThinCustom` (a hidden base material plus a lightweight instance). `Instance` is the old spelling of `ThinCustom` and still works, with a warning.

codes.title: '#pragma material' configures a material, and this file has no 'export void Name(inout material m)' entry to configure.
codes.meaning: The file has `#pragma material(...)` and no material entry to configure. A function library does not become a `UMaterial`, so the settings have nothing to apply to.
codes.fix: Delete the pragma, or add the `export void Name(inout material m)` the file was meant to have.

codes.title: 'Backend = Instance' is the old spelling of 'Backend = ThinCustom'; write the new one.
codes.meaning: `Backend = Instance` — the 1.x deprecation-window spelling of `ThinCustom`.
codes.fix: Write `Backend = ThinCustom`. Nothing changes about what is produced.

codes.title: '#pragma material' takes 'Key = Value' pairs; '{0}' has no key.
codes.meaning: `#pragma material` was given something without a key.
codes.fix: Write `Key = Value`. The keys are the `UMaterial` property names; unknown ones are passed through to the material by reflection, so a misspelt key is reported by the emitter and not here.

codes.title: '{0}' is a compile-time constant, and this initializer is not one; a constant is built from literals and other constants.
codes.meaning: A `static const` (or `const`) has an initializer the binder cannot fold to a value. A constant becomes a Constant node in the graph, so its value has to exist before anything runs.
codes.fix: Build it from literals and other constants. A value that depends on a `uniform`, a texture sample or a node is not a constant — declare it as an ordinary local.

codes.title: '{0}' is a file-scope variable with no storage class; write 'uniform' for a material parameter or 'static const' for a compile-time constant.
codes.meaning: A file-scope variable has no storage class: `float Gain = 1.0;` or `static float …`. Neither has a node. A file-scope value is either an input to the material (`uniform`) or a constant folded into it (`static const`).
codes.fix: Write `uniform` or `static const`. `const` alone is accepted and means the same as `static const`.

codes.title: A file-scope variable of type {0} has no node; a 'uniform' or 'static const' must be numeric, bool, a texture or a sampler.
codes.meaning: A file-scope variable has a type with no node: a `material`, a `Substrate` value, a user `struct`, `void`.
codes.fix: A `material` is produced by the entry, not declared; a `struct` is a compile-time aggregate and lives inside a function; a `Substrate` value comes from a `Substrate.` node.

codes.title: A texture uniform has no HLSL initializer; write its default asset as '/// @default /Game/...'.
codes.meaning: A texture `uniform` has an HLSL initializer. A texture has no literal value.
codes.fix: Write its default asset as `/// @default /Game/Textures/T_Name` above the declaration, and leave the declaration itself as plain legal HLSL.

codes.title: '{0}' is a compile-time constant and must be initialised where it is declared.
codes.meaning: A `static const` — at file scope or inside a function — has no initializer.
codes.fix: Initialise it where it is declared, or drop `const` to make it an ordinary variable.

codes.title: '@layer' and '@layerblend' make two different assets; a function is one or the other.
codes.meaning: One function carries both `@layer` and `@layerblend`. They select two different asset classes.
codes.fix: Keep the one that matches the signature: `@layer` for `void (inout material)`, `@layerblend` for `void (material …, inout material)`.

codes.title: A 'uniform' array has no parameter node; declare one uniform per element, or make it 'static const'.
codes.meaning: A `uniform` is declared as an array. There is no array parameter node.
codes.fix: Declare one uniform per element, or make it `static const` if the values are fixed, or use a texture for a table that has to be read at run time.

codes.title: '@slider' takes two numbers, a minimum and a maximum; '{0}' is not that.
codes.meaning: `@slider` is not two numbers, or its minimum is not below its maximum.
codes.fix: Write `/// @slider 0 4`.

codes.title: '@sort' takes one whole number; '{0}' is not that.
codes.meaning: `@sort` is not one whole number.
codes.fix: Write `/// @sort 3`. Without it, parameters sort in declaration order.

codes.title: '@sampler' needs a sampler type after it, such as 'Color', 'Normal' or 'LinearColor'.
codes.meaning: `@sampler` has no value.
codes.fix: Name a sampler type: `Color`, `Normal`, `LinearColor`, `Grayscale`, `Masks`, … The list comes from the engine, so an unknown spelling is reported by the emitter and not here.

codes.title: '@static' asks for a static switch and is only meaningful on a 'uniform bool'.
codes.meaning: `@static` sits on something that is not a `uniform bool`. It asks for a static switch, which only a boolean parameter can become.
codes.fix: Delete the directive, or change the declaration to `uniform bool`.

codes.title: '@{0}' means nothing here; it belongs on {1}.
codes.meaning: A `///` directive is written on a declaration where it cannot mean anything: `@slider` on a function, `@library` on a uniform, `@sampler` on something that is not a texture, `@asset` on a function that is not an `extern` prototype, `@library` or `@name` on a function that is not `export`. It is dropped.
codes.fix: Move it to the declaration it belongs to, or delete it. Unknown keys are **not** this warning — they are passed through to the node by reflection.

codes.title: '@static {0}' does not name a parameter of '{1}'.
codes.meaning: `@param <name>` names something that is not a parameter of the function. Usually the parameter was renamed and the comment was not.
codes.fix: Correct the name, or delete the line.

codes.title: '@custom {0}' is not a modifier this language knows; the only one is 'selfcontained'.
codes.meaning: `@custom` is followed by a word that is not a modifier it knows.
codes.fix: The only modifier is `selfcontained`. `Inline`, the 1.x spelling, is gone.

codes.title: '@{0}' needs a value after it.
codes.meaning: A directive that needs a value has none: `@name`, `@asset`, `@library`, `@default`, or `@param` without a parameter name.
codes.fix: Write the value after the key. A directive's value runs to the next ` @` or to the end of the line.

codes.title: '@custom' on '{0}' did not make its body opaque; the directive has to sit in the '///' block directly above the declaration.
codes.meaning: `@custom` was recorded on a function whose body was parsed as DreamShaderLang rather than captured verbatim. The parser only makes a body opaque when it sees `@custom` in the `///` block **directly above** the declaration.
codes.fix: Move the `@custom` line so nothing separates it from the declaration.

codes.title: '@{0}' is written twice in this block; the last one wins.
codes.meaning: One key appears twice in one `///` block. The last one wins.
codes.fix: Delete the earlier one. `@param` is the one key that may legitimately repeat and never reports this.

codes.title: '#pragma layout' expects a whole number for '{0}'; '{1}' was ignored.
codes.meaning: A `#pragma layout(...)` line could not be read: no `Node`/`Comment` selector, an unknown key, or a coordinate that is not a whole number. The line is ignored and nothing else is affected.
codes.fix: Layout is written by the decompiler and is rarely edited by hand; the shape is `#pragma layout(Node, Var = UV, X = -1100, Y = -120)` and `#pragma layout(Comment, Text = "Sampling", X = …, Y = …, Width = …, Height = …)`. A node with no layout entry is simply placed by the layout pass.

codes.title: '@static {0}' makes a parameter a static bool pin, which only a 'bool' input can be, and '{0}' is {1}.
codes.meaning: `/// @static <Parameter>` on a function makes that parameter a StaticBool pin -- a pin whose value picks a shader permutation -- and the parameter named is not a `bool`.
codes.fix: Name a `bool` parameter, or remove the directive.

codes.title: 'Substrate = {0}' is not a Substrate mode; the modes are 'Legacy', 'Bridge' and 'Native'.
codes.meaning: `#pragma material(Substrate = ...)` (or the `Substrate` setting of a 1.x `Shader`) names something other than the three modes.
codes.fix: Write `Legacy` (the default: built as written, the engine converts), `Bridge` (the legacy attributes become one `Substrate.ShadingModels` node in a Substrate project) or `Native` (the source is Substrate source).

codes.title: A slider range ('@slider', or 'Slider(min, max)' in a 1.x property) is for a scalar parameter; this one is '{0}', which has no slider, so the range is ignored.
codes.meaning: A slider range -- `/// @slider min max` on a `uniform`, or `Slider(min, max)` in the metadata of a 1.x property -- sits on a parameter that is not a scalar: a vector (`float3`, `vec3`, `float4`), a texture, or a `bool` (a static switch). The range is the `SliderMin` / `SliderMax` of a ScalarParameter, and none of those parameters has a slider, so it has nowhere to go and is dropped. The compile goes on.
codes.fix: Remove the range, or put it on a scalar `float`, `half` or `int` parameter -- for a colour that should stay in a range, one scalar per channel, or a scalar that scales the colour.

codes.title: '{0}' asks to generate '{1}', and only a package's header generates material functions; this file is not in one, so nothing is generated. Write an 'export' function (or a 1.x ShaderFunction) to make a material function of your own.
codes.meaning: A function carries `@generate` -- a 2.0 `/// @generate` or a 1.x `Generate =` header -- in a file that is not in a package. Only a package's header generates material functions ([Packages ▸ Asset headers](../tools/packages.md#asset-headers)); anywhere else the annotation does nothing.
codes.fix: To make a material function of the project's own, write an `export` function in a `.dss` (or a 1.x `ShaderFunction` in a `.dsf`). If the header is meant to be a package's, install it under `DShader/Packages`.

codes.title: '#pragma nogeneration' in '{0}' was ignored: it marks the file it is written in, a header builds nothing, and the files that include it are not marked by it. Write it in each of those files instead.
codes.meaning: `#pragma nogeneration` *(after 2.1.2)* stands in a header. It marks the file it is written in; a header builds nothing, and the files that include it are not marked by it.
codes.fix: Write the pragma in each source that should be NoGeneration, or `/// @nogeneration` above one of its exports.

codes.title: A 'disable_warning' or 'disable_error' list names no code, and disables nothing; write the codes after it, such as 'DSH7224'.
codes.meaning: A `disable_warning` or `disable_error` list *(after 2.1.2)* holds a word that is not a diagnostic code (`DSH` and four digits), or no code at all. The word is ignored; a list never means "everything". See [Disabling diagnostics](../language-v2/disable-diagnostics.md).
codes.fix: Write the codes as they are reported, such as `DSH7224`, separated by commas or spaces.

codes.title: A '.dsi' needs one '#pragma instance(Parent = "...")' naming the material it is an instance of, and this file has none.
codes.meaning: A `.dsi` file has no `#pragma instance(...)`. The pragma is what makes the file an instance and says of what.
codes.fix: Add `#pragma instance(Parent = "M_Parent")` at the top: a bare name for a source beside this file, or an object path for any material.

codes.title: '#pragma instance' is written a second time, and one '.dsi' is one material instance; the line {0} already declares it.
codes.meaning: A `.dsi` has two `#pragma instance` lines. One file is one instance.
codes.fix: Merge the keys into one pragma, or split the file.

codes.title: 'Parent' in '#pragma instance' names the material this is an instance of, and it is empty.
codes.meaning: `#pragma instance` has no `Parent`, or `Parent` is there and empty. An instance is nothing but overrides of one parent.
codes.fix: Name the parent: a DreamShader material by its name, or any material or instance by object path -- `#pragma instance(Parent = "M_Skin")`.

codes.title: '{0}' is set twice by '#pragma instance'; it was already set on line {1}.
codes.meaning: One key is written twice in `#pragma instance(...)`.
codes.fix: Keep one.

codes.title: A '.dsi' is configured by '#pragma instance', and '#pragma material' configures a material; write these keys in '#pragma instance(...)'.
codes.meaning: A `.dsi` holds something an instance has no use for: `#pragma material(...)` (that pragma configures a material being built), a declaration that is not a `uniform`, a function, a `struct`, or an `#include`. An instance has no graph; it only assigns parameters of its parent.
codes.fix: Move pragma keys into `#pragma instance(...)` -- only properties an instance can override are accepted there (`BlendMode`, `TwoSided`, `ShadingModel`, `OpacityMaskClipValue`, ...; see `Docs/language-v2/instances.md`). Move functions and types to a `.dss` or a `.dsh`, and remove includes.

codes.title: '#pragma instance' declares a material instance and belongs in a '.dsi' file of its own, and this line is in '{0}'; move it and its overrides into a '.dsi'.
codes.meaning: `#pragma instance` stands in a `.dss` (or a header). A material and its instances are separate assets and separate files.
codes.fix: Move the pragma and the overrides below it into a `.dsi` of their own.

codes.title: '{0}' overrides a {1} parameter and needs the value it is set to, as 'uniform {2} {0} = ...;', and it has no initializer.
codes.meaning: An override of a scalar, vector or switch parameter has no initializer, so there is no value to set.
codes.fix: Write the value: `uniform float Gain = 2.0;`.

codes.title: '{0}' overrides a {1} parameter, which takes an asset rather than an HLSL value; write '/// @default /Game/...' (or '/// @default None') above it instead of an initializer.
codes.meaning: An override of a texture (or font, runtime virtual texture, collection ...) parameter is given an initializer, or has no `/// @default`. An asset is not an HLSL value; it is named by the directive, exactly as in the parent.
codes.fix: Write `/// @default /Game/Textures/T_Override` above `uniform Texture2D Name;`, or `/// @default None` to clear it.

codes.title: '{0}' is not a parameter of the parent '{1}'.
codes.meaning: The `.dsi` overrides a name that is not a parameter of its parent. Either the name is wrong, or the parent declares that uniform and never reads it, in which case the material has no such parameter.
codes.fix: Use the parameter's name as the parent's Details panel shows it (`/// @name` on the override when it is not an identifier). `dsc index` lists a parent's parameters.

codes.title: '{0}' is a {1} parameter of type '{2}' in the parent, and this override declares '{3}'.
codes.meaning: The override declares another type than the parent's parameter has: `float3` for a scalar parameter, `bool` without `@static` for a static switch, `Texture2D` for a cube texture.
codes.fix: Declare the override exactly as the parent declares the uniform.

codes.title: '/// @static' on an instance override means a static switch ('uniform bool') or a static component mask ('uniform bool4'), and '{0}' is declared '{1}'.
codes.meaning: `/// @static` and the parent disagree. The directive stands on an override that is neither `uniform bool` (a static switch) nor `uniform bool4` (a static component mask); or the parent's parameter is static and the override lacks `/// @static`; or the parent sets the parameter at run time and the override asks for a static one.
codes.fix: Declare the override the way the parent declares the parameter: add or remove `/// @static`, or fix the type.

codes.title: '{0}' is overridden a second time, and one instance sets a parameter once; the override on line {1} already sets it.
codes.meaning: One parameter is overridden twice in a `.dsi`.
codes.fix: Keep one of the two lines.

codes.title: '@{0}' has no effect above '#pragma instance', where only '@name' is read; remove it.
codes.meaning: A directive that describes a parameter (`@group`, `@sort`, `@slider`, `@desc`, `@default` on a value) stands on an instance override or above the pragma. That metadata belongs to the parent; an instance only sets values.
codes.fix: Remove it. `@name`, `@static`, `@default` (on an asset override) and `@page` are the directives a `.dsi` reads.

codes.title: The parameters of the parent are not available here, so the names and types of these overrides are checked only for their shape; compile the parent first, or check the file in the editor.
codes.meaning: The parent's parameters could not be looked up where this file was bound -- the parent is an asset path and no editor is attached (a language-service check), or the parent source has not been compiled yet -- so override names and types are checked for their shape only.
codes.fix: Nothing to fix. Compile the parent first, or check the file with the editor running, to have every name verified.

codes.title: '{0}' matches the parent parameter '{1}' only in case, and DreamShader names are case-sensitive; write '{1}'.
codes.meaning: An override matches a parent parameter only when case is ignored. Parameter names are case-sensitive in the engine, so the override would silently set nothing.
codes.fix: Spell the name exactly as the parent does.

codes.title: '{0}' is set to a value the compiler can fold, a literal or an expression over literals, and this initializer is not one.
codes.meaning: An override's value is not something the compiler can evaluate: it reads a variable, calls a node, or uses a run-time function. An instance stores constants.
codes.fix: Use a literal or arithmetic over literals: `uniform float3 Tint = float3(1, 0.5, 0) * 0.5;`.

codes.title: '@page' takes one whole number of zero or more, and '{0}' is not that.
codes.meaning: `/// @page` is not a whole number of zero or more, or it stands on an override that is not a Font.
codes.fix: Write the font page index above a Font override -- `/// @page 2` -- and nowhere else.

codes.title: '#pragma {0}' boxes or places graph nodes, and a '.dsi' has no graph; the line was ignored.
codes.meaning: `#pragma region` or `#pragma layout` stands in a `.dsi`. Both arrange graph nodes, and an instance has no graph.
codes.fix: Remove the line.

codes.title: '{0}' exists in the parent only as a layer or blend parameter, and a '.dsi' overrides global parameters only.
codes.meaning: The name exists in the parent only as a parameter of a material layer or blend. A `.dsi` sets global parameters; layer parameters are associated with a layer index the file has no syntax for.
codes.fix: Override it on the instance asset by hand, or expose the value as a global parameter in the parent.

codes.title: '{0}' is an array, and an instance override assigns one parameter; override each element's parameter on its own.
codes.meaning: An override is declared as an array, or with a type that is no material parameter type. Each parameter of a material is one name and one value: a number, a bool, a texture, or one of `RuntimeVirtualTexture`, `SparseVolumeTexture`, `TextureCollection`, `ParameterCollection` and `Font`.
codes.fix: Override each element's parameter on its own line, with the type the parent declares it with.

codes.title: '#pragma instance' takes 'Key = Value' pairs, and '{0}' has no key.
codes.meaning: `#pragma instance(...)` contains a bare value. Every entry is `Key = Value`.
codes.fix: Write, for example, `#pragma instance(Parent = "M_Base", TwoSided = true)`.

codes.title: '{0}' is not a key of '#pragma pipeline'; the keys are {1}.
codes.meaning: `#pragma pipeline(...)` has a key that is not one of its five: `Order`, `Injection`, `Views`, `Requires` and `Enabled`. Keys are case-sensitive, and a spelling that differs only in case is suggested. A buffer's or a pass's key (`Scale`, `Material`) is not a pipeline key either.
codes.fix: Correct the key, or move it where it belongs: buffer keys go in `buffer Name : Format(Key = Value)`, pass keys inside the `pass` block.

codes.title: '{0}' is set twice by '#pragma pipeline'; it was already set on line {1}.
codes.meaning: One key is written twice in `#pragma pipeline(...)`. Keys are compared case-sensitively, so `order` beside `Order` is DSH7300, not this.
codes.fix: Keep one of the two.

codes.title:
A key of `#pragma pipeline` has a value it cannot take; the message says which:

- `Order` is not a whole number, or is quoted.
codes.meaning:
A key of `#pragma pipeline` has a value it cannot take; the message says which:

- `Order` is not a whole number, or is quoted. It orders the pipelines that have passes at one injection point, smaller first.
- `Views` or `Requires` is quoted (`Views = "Game"`): both take names written without quotes, and a quoted value is refused rather than dropped, which would leave the pipeline on its default views or requirements. `Views = ""` has a message of its own: it names no view, so the pipeline would run nowhere.
- `Views` or `Requires` names a word that is not one of its own. `Views` takes `Game`, `Editor`, `SceneCapture`, `PlanarReflection`, `ReflectionCapture` and `Thumbnail`; `Requires` takes `PostProcess`, `SceneResolve` and `CustomStencil`. A case-only match is suggested.
- `Enabled` is not a name: it takes a `uniform bool` of the file, or `true`.
codes.fix:
Write the values without quotes, the words of `Views` and `Requires` joined by `|`:

```hlsl
#pragma pipeline(Order = 100, Views = Game | Editor, Requires = PostProcess, Enabled = bShowOutline)
```

A pipeline that should not run is switched off through `Enabled` and a `uniform bool`, not by an empty `Views`.

codes.title: '{0}' is not an injection point; the points are {1}.
codes.meaning: `Injection` -- of `#pragma pipeline` or of a pass -- names no injection point. The names are case-sensitive, and the points on the post-process chain carry its prefix: `AfterDOF` is suggested as `PostProcess.AfterDOF`.
codes.fix: Use one of the points the message lists, spelled as listed and, in a pass, without quotes: `Injection = PostProcess.AfterDOF;`. What each point sees is in `Docs/language-v2/passes.md`.

codes.title: '{0}' is not a pass kind; a pass is {1}.
codes.meaning: A `pass` header names a kind that does not exist. The kinds are `fullscreen`, `compute`, `mesh`, `clear` and `copy`, written in lower case; `Fullscreen` is suggested as `fullscreen`. Without a kind, the pass's keys and the rules that depend on the kind are not checked.
codes.fix: Write one of the five: `pass Blur : compute { ... }`.

codes.title: '{0}' is not a buffer format; the formats are {1}.
codes.meaning: A `buffer` declaration names a format that does not exist. The formats are `R8`, `RG8`, `RGBA8`, `R16F`, `RG16F`, `RGBA16F`, `R32F`, `RG32F`, `RGBA32F`, `R32U`, `RG32U` and `Depth32`, case-sensitive; engine spellings such as `PF_R8` or `R8_UNORM` are not among them.
codes.fix: Write one of them: `buffer Mask : R8;`. `R32U` and `RG32U` are reserved (DSH7321), and `Depth32` is only a mesh pass's own depth (DSH7330).

codes.title: '{0}' is not a key of a buffer; the keys are {1}.
codes.meaning: A buffer's argument list has a key that is not a buffer key. The keys are `Scale`, `Size`, `Resolution`, `Clear`, `Mips`, `History` and `Export`, case-sensitive. The format is not a key: it is written after the colon.
codes.fix: Correct the key: `buffer Blurred : R8(Scale = 0.5, Export = true);`.

codes.title: '{0}' is set twice for buffer '{1}'; it was already set on line {2}.
codes.meaning: One key is written twice in a buffer's argument list.
codes.fix: Keep one of the two.

codes.title: A buffer key has a value it cannot take; the message says which.
codes.meaning:
A buffer key has a value it cannot take; the message says which. Numbers are folded when the pipeline compiles, so a `static const` works and a `uniform` does not.

- `Scale` is not a number, or is outside 0.0625 to 4.
- `Size` is not two whole numbers, or a side is outside 1 to 16384.
- `Resolution` is not `Render` or `Output`. `Resolution = Fixed` is refused too: a fixed size is written `Size = int2(w, h)`.
- `Clear` is not a number, a `float2` to `float4`, or `None`.
- `Mips` is not the integer `1`. Passes cannot initialize or update a mip chain yet.
- `History` or `Export` is not `true` or `false`.
codes.fix:
Write the value the message asks for:

```hlsl
buffer Wind : RG16F(Size = int2(256, 256), Clear = 0, History = true, Export = true);
```

codes.title: 'Size' gives buffer '{0}' a fixed size, so '{1}' has nothing to say; remove one of them.
codes.meaning: A buffer has `Size` and `Scale` (or `Resolution`). `Size` makes it a fixed number of texels; `Scale` and `Resolution` size it after the view, so one of the two has nothing to say.
codes.fix: Remove `Size` from a buffer that follows the view, or `Scale` and `Resolution` from a fixed one.

codes.title: '{0}' is not a key of a {1} pass; its keys are {2}.
codes.meaning: A pass has a key that no kind of pass has. Every pass takes `Injection` and `Enabled`; beyond those, `fullscreen` takes `Material`, `Shader`, `Entry`; `compute` takes `Shader`, `Entry`, `Threads`, `Dispatch`; `mesh` takes `Filter`, `Material`, `Mode`, `Depth`, `Cull`, `Blend`, `Usage`, `Nanite`, `NaniteValue`; `clear` takes `Value`; `copy` takes none. Keys are case-sensitive, and a case-only match is suggested.
codes.fix: Correct the key. A binding is not a key: it starts with `read`, `write` or `param`.

codes.title: '{0}' is a key of {1} passes, and '{2}' is a {3} pass.
codes.meaning: A pass has a key of another kind of pass -- `Threads` in a `fullscreen` pass, `Filter` in a `compute` one, `Value` in a `copy`. The message names a kind the key belongs to.
codes.fix: Remove the key, or change the pass's kind if the key is what was meant.

codes.title: '{0}' is set twice in pass '{1}'; it was already set on line {2}.
codes.meaning: One key is written twice in one pass. Keys are compared case-sensitively, so `injection` beside `Injection` is DSH7310, not this.
codes.fix: Keep one of the two.

codes.title: A pass key has a value it cannot take; the message says which.
codes.meaning:
A pass key has a value it cannot take; the message says which. Numbers are folded when the pipeline compiles, so a `static const` works and a `uniform` does not.

- `Injection` is quoted or is not a name; `Enabled` is neither `true` nor a name (a number, a quoted string).
- `Material` or `Shader` is not a quoted, non-empty string; `Entry` is not a function name.
- `Threads` is not two or three whole numbers, at least 1 each way, at most 64 in z and 1024 in all.
- `Dispatch` is not a buffer, `<buffer> * n` or `<buffer> / n` with a positive `n`, or two or three whole numbers of at least 1.
- `Mode`, `Depth`, `Cull`, `Blend` or `Nanite` is not one of its words, or is quoted; `Depth = Own(...)` does not hold exactly one buffer name.
- `Usage` is not usages joined by `|`, or names one that does not exist (`Splines` is suggested as `SplineMesh`).
- `Nanite = AssignStencil(n)` has no single `n` from 1 to 255; `Nanite = StencilMask` stands in a pass whose `Filter` has no `Stencil(...)` term to mask by.
- `NaniteValue` (mesh) or `Value` (clear) is not one to four numbers.
- The value or the mask of a `Stencil(...)` filter term is not a whole number.
codes.fix: Write the value in the form the message gives. A pass that selects by layer or list and wants its Nanite members covered uses `Nanite = AssignStencil(n)`, which gives them custom stencil `n`.

codes.title: A filter joins its terms with '|' (either) and '&' (both), and nothing else.
codes.fix:
Build the filter from the three terms; `&` binds tighter than `|`:

```hlsl
Filter = Stencil(4, 0x0F) | Layer(Enemies | Allies) & List(Visible);
```

codes.title: Mesh pass '{0}' needs 'Filter = ...' to say which primitives it draws: 'Stencil(1)', 'Layer(Name)', 'List(Name)'.
codes.fix: Add the key: `Material = "PP_Composite";`, or `Shader = "BoxBlur.usf";` with `Entry = BlurCS;`, or the pass's HLSL in an `hlsl { ... }` block of its own, or `Filter = Layer(Highlight);`. A mesh pass that draws each primitive with its own material says `Mode = Own` (the default without a `Material`).

codes.title: Fullscreen pass '{0}' draws a 'Material' or runs a 'Shader', and it names both.
codes.meaning: Two keys of a `fullscreen` pass contradict each other. Two messages: the pass names both a `Material` and a `Shader`, and it either draws the one or runs the other; or it names a `Material` and an `Entry`, which is a function of a shader file.
codes.fix: Keep `Material` for a Post Process material, or `Shader` with `Entry` for HLSL, and remove the other.

codes.title: A fullscreen material pass writes exactly one buffer, as 'write Buffer;', and '{0}' writes {1}.
'{0}.Previous' is last frame's contents, which nothing writes any more; write '{0}'.
codes.meaning: A pass writes `B.Previous`. That is last frame's contents of a `History = true` buffer, which only a `read` can name; this frame's writes go to `B`, which is next frame's `.Previous`.
codes.fix: Write `B`: `write Result = Wind;` beside `read Previous = Wind.Previous;`.

codes.title: '{0}' is bound twice in pass '{1}'; inside a pass every input, output and parameter has a name of its own.
codes.fix:
Rename one of the two:

```hlsl
read  Source = Mask;
param Width  = OutlineWidth;   // not 'SourceSize', which the slot gives the size of 'Source'
```

codes.title: '{0}' is an array, and a pipeline has no array parameters or constants; declare one per element.
'{0}' is an integer format, which no pass can read or write yet: HLSL passes see float4 textures, and materials and mesh passes write floats. Use 'R32F' or 'RG32F' (an id is exact up to 16777216).
codes.meaning: A buffer is declared `R32U` or `RG32U`. No pass can use an integer buffer yet: an HLSL slot declares its inputs `Texture2D<float4>` and its compute outputs `RWTexture2D<float4>`, which an integer view does not match, and materials, mesh passes, exports and the visualizer read and write floats.
codes.fix: Use `R32F` or `RG32F`. A float holds a whole number exactly up to 16777216 (2^24), enough for an object id.

codes.title: 'Enabled' is false, so this would never run, and a pipeline asset has no switch that is always off; drive it with a 'uniform bool', or comment the declaration out.
codes.meaning: `Enabled` -- of `#pragma pipeline` or of a pass -- is `false`, or a `static const bool` that folds to `false`. A pipeline asset has no switch that is always off: the pipeline or the pass would never run.

codes.title: A fullscreen material pass needs the scene textures, which do not exist yet at {0}; run '{1}' at AfterBasePass or later.
codes.fix: Move the pass: a fullscreen material to `AfterBasePass` or later (`BeforePostProcess` is where it is known to work), a mesh pass to a point from `BeforeBasePass` to `PostProcess.AfterFXAA`. Work that has to run at `BeginView` is a `compute` pass, or a `fullscreen` pass with `Shader`.

codes.title: At AfterBasePass scene colour holds the emissive light only; nothing is lit yet, so pass '{0}' {1} that.
codes.fix: Nothing has to change if that is what the pass means to see. Otherwise move it to a later point, or give a mesh pass at `BeforeBasePass` `Depth = None` or `Depth = Own(...)`. A mesh pass with its own depth that has to run in split screen or in stereo writes a buffer of the pipeline instead of the scene's texture, for a later pass to bring into the scene, or tests against the scene depth.

codes.title: 'CustomStencil' is the stencil half of the custom depth texture, which no pass can bind as a texture of its own, and pass '{0}' {1} it; read it through the scene textures instead: a SceneTexture node in the material, CalcSceneCustomStencil in a '.usf'.
codes.fix: Run the pass at a point where the texture exists. Custom stencil is read through the scene textures: a `SceneTexture` node in the material (`UE.SceneTexture(SceneTextureId = CustomStencil)`), `CalcSceneCustomStencil` in a `.usf`.

Write a buffer of the pipeline instead, or move the pass to where the texture is writable: `Translucency` at `PostProcess.TranslucencyAfterDOF`, `SceneColor` at any other point from `AfterBasePass` on.

codes.title: '{0}' exists at AfterBasePass only when r.CustomDepth.Order draws custom depth before the base pass; where it does not, pass '{1}' reads a cleared placeholder. From AfterOpaque on it always exists.
codes.meaning: A pass at `AfterBasePass` reads `CustomDepth`, which is drawn before the base pass only when `r.CustomDepth.Order` says so: `0`, or the default `2` with DBuffer decals on. With `1`, or `2` without DBuffer decals, the pass reads a cleared placeholder.
codes.fix: Nothing to fix where the project draws custom depth first. Otherwise run the pass at `AfterOpaque` or later, where custom depth always exists.

codes.title: 'Depth = Own({0})' tests against a depth of this pipeline's own, and '{0}' is a built-in texture; declare 'buffer MyDepth : Depth32;', or write 'Depth = TestScene'.
Pass '{0}' reads '{1}', which no pass writes, and '{1}' is 'Clear = None', so what it reads is undefined.
codes.meaning: A pass reads a buffer declared `Clear = None` before any pass has written it, in frame order (injection point, then declaration order). Two messages: no pass writes it at all, or its first writer runs after the reader. With no clear value, what such a read sees is undefined.
codes.fix: Move the reader after the writer, give the buffer a `Clear` value (`Clear = 0` is the default), or read last frame's `B.Previous` of a `History = true` buffer.

codes.title: Pass '{0}' reads '{1}' before '{2}' writes it in the frame, so it reads the buffer's 'Clear' value; move the reader after the writer, or read '{1}.Previous'.
codes.meaning: A pass reads a buffer before the first pass that writes it, in frame order (injection point, then declaration order), so it reads the buffer's `Clear` value rather than what that writer draws. Often the two passes sit at injection points in the wrong order.
codes.fix: Move the reader after the writer -- later in the file, or at a later injection point. A reader that means last frame's contents reads `B.Previous` of a `History = true` buffer.

codes.title: Pass '{0}' reads and writes '{1}', and one pass cannot have one texture as its input and its output; write another buffer, or read '{1}.Previous' of a 'History = true' buffer.
codes.meaning: A pass reads and writes the same texture, and one GPU pass cannot have one texture as its input and its output. `B.Previous` and `B` are two textures and do not count. Nor does the chain's colour: a pass of any kind -- a `fullscreen` or `compute` pass, or a `copy` -- may read `SceneColor` while it writes it, and `Translucency` at `PostProcess.TranslucencyAfterDOF`, because a pass that writes it draws into a scratch texture that is brought back afterwards.
codes.fix: Write another buffer and read that in a later pass, or read `B.Previous` of a `History = true` buffer.

codes.title: '{0}' reads no UserSceneTexture of '{1}': its inputs are {2}.
codes.meaning: A `fullscreen` pass binds `read X = B`, and its material has no `UE.UserSceneTexture` named `X`; the message lists the names it has. `X` is the name in the material, `B` the buffer of the pipeline, and `read B;` is short for `read B = B;`. An instance's renamed inputs count under their new names. A `dsc check` of a `.dsp` whose material has never been built reads the material's inputs off its source, and does not see a `UE.UserSceneTexture` inside a material function it calls.
codes.fix:
Bind to a name the material reads -- `read Mask = Blurred;` -- or add the node to the material:

```hlsl
float Halo = UE.UserSceneTexture(UserSceneTexture = "Blurred", Coordinates = UV).Color.r;
```

codes.title: '{0}' reads the UserSceneTexture '{1}', and pass '{2}' binds nothing to it, so it samples black; add 'read {1} = <Buffer>;'.
codes.meaning: The material of a `fullscreen` pass reads a `UE.UserSceneTexture` the pass binds no buffer to. The engine still gives the input a slot, and it samples black.
codes.fix: Bind it -- `read <Name> = <Buffer>;` -- or remove the node from the material.

codes.title: Fullscreen material pass '{0}' reads {1} buffers, and a post-process material has {2} input slots, shared with its own SceneTexture nodes; split the pass in two, or write it with 'Shader =' (a '.usf' pass reads up to {3}).
codes.meaning: A `fullscreen` pass with `Material` needs more inputs than a Post Process material has. The engine gives it five post-process input slots, shared: every `SceneTexture` node reading `PostProcessInput0` to `PostProcessInput4` takes one, and every `UE.UserSceneTexture` input of the material, bound or not, takes one of the rest. Two messages: the pass reads more than five buffers; or the material's `UserSceneTexture` inputs do not fit beside its own `SceneTexture` nodes -- a material that reads `PostProcessInput0` for the scene colour has four left.
codes.fix: Read fewer buffers in one pass: split it in two, or pack several channels into one buffer. Or write the pass with `Shader =`; a `.usf` pass reads up to eight.

codes.title: '{0}' is a {1} material, and a fullscreen pass draws a Post Process one: '#pragma material(Domain = PostProcess)'.
codes.meaning: A `fullscreen` pass draws a material whose domain is not Post Process. The pass runs the material through the engine's post-process material pass, which draws only that domain.
codes.fix: Give the material `#pragma material(Domain = PostProcess)`.

codes.title: Pass '{0}' writes a data buffer, and '{1}' scales what it reads and writes by the exposure; give it '#pragma material(bDisablePreExposureScale = true)'.
codes.meaning: A `fullscreen` pass with `Material` writes a buffer of the pipeline rather than the scene colour, and the material leaves pre-exposure on. The engine then scales what the material reads and writes by the exposure, so a mask or a vector stored in the buffer changes with the scene's brightness.
codes.fix:
Turn it off in the material's `.dss`:

```hlsl
#pragma material(Domain = PostProcess, bDisablePreExposureScale = true)
```

codes.title: '{0}' is compiled for BlendableLocation {1}, and pass '{2}' runs it at {3}, {4} tonemapping, so its colours are in another space than it expects; use {5}.
codes.meaning: A `fullscreen` pass runs its material on the other side of tonemapping from the `BlendableLocation` it is compiled for, so its colours are in another space than it expects: a material compiled for `SceneColorAfterTonemapping` -- the engine's default -- or `ReplacingTonemapper` at a point before tonemapping, or one compiled for another location at `PostProcess.ReplaceTonemapper`, `PostProcess.AfterTonemap`, `PostProcess.AfterFXAA` or `EndOfView`.
codes.fix:
Give the material the location that matches the pass's injection point -- `SceneColorAfterDOF` or `SceneColorBeforeDOF` before tonemapping, `SceneColorAfterTonemapping` after it:

```hlsl
#pragma material(Domain = PostProcess, BlendableLocation = SceneColorAfterDOF)
```

codes.title: '{0}' has no UE.DreamPassOutput in its graph, so a mesh pass has nothing to write; add 'UE.DreamPassOutput(Output0 = ...);' to the material.
codes.meaning: A `mesh` pass's override `Material` has no `UE.DreamPassOutput` in its own graph. The node is what a mesh pass writes its outputs from, and what makes the engine compile the mesh pass's shaders for the material at all; one inside a material function the material calls does not count (DSH5302). Checked on Unreal Engine 5.8 and later, where the Custom Pass runtime is.
codes.fix:
Add the node to the material:

```hlsl
UE.DreamPassOutput(Output0 = float4(1, 0, 0, 0));
```

codes.title: '{0}' leaves Output{1} of its UE.DreamPassOutput unconnected, so '{2}' would receive nothing.
codes.meaning: A `mesh` pass writes an output of `UE.DreamPassOutput` -- `write Output1 = Id;` -- whose pin its material leaves unconnected, so the buffer would receive nothing.
codes.fix: Connect the pin in the material -- `UE.DreamPassOutput(Output0 = Mask, Output1 = Id);` -- or remove the write the material does not fill.

codes.title: Mesh pass '{0}' draws {1} primitives, and '{2}' is not compiled for them; give the material its usage flag ('#pragma material({3} = true)' in its '.dss'), or leave {1} out of 'Usage'.
codes.meaning: A `mesh` pass draws primitives of a kind its override material is not compiled for. The pass's `Usage` -- `StaticMesh | InstancedStaticMeshes | SkeletalMesh` when it is not written -- lists what it draws, and each kind needs the material's usage flag; `Landscape` needs none. The message names the missing flag. Checked on Unreal Engine 5.8 and later, where the Custom Pass runtime is.
codes.fix:
Set the flag in the material's `.dss`, or narrow `Usage` to what the pass meets (`Usage = StaticMesh | InstancedStaticMeshes;`):

```hlsl
#pragma material(ShadingModel = Unlit, bUsedWithSkeletalMesh = true, bUsedWithInstancedStaticMeshes = true)
```

codes.title: Mesh pass '{0}' writes '{1}', a texture of the scene, together with '{2}', a buffer of the pipeline. A mesh pass draws all its targets through one viewport, so they have to be one size holding the view at one place; the scene's textures are usually larger than the view they hold (rounded up, and in the editor grown to the largest view so far) while a buffer is the view's size, and the runtime skips the pass whenever the two differ. Write them in two mesh passes.
codes.fix: Give the outputs one `Scale`, `Resolution` or `Size`, and an own depth their resolution and a scale (or a fixed size) no smaller than theirs; for a smaller result, draw at full size and `copy` into a smaller buffer afterwards. Write a texture of the scene and a buffer of the pipeline in two mesh passes.

codes.title: '{0}' is a {1} material, and a mesh pass draws primitives with a Surface one.
codes.meaning: A `mesh` pass's override `Material` is not a Surface material -- a Post Process, a decal, a UI material. A mesh pass draws primitives with it, as their own materials draw them.
codes.fix: Make the override a Surface material (the default domain: remove `Domain` from its `#pragma material`). A Post Process material is drawn by a `fullscreen` pass.

codes.title: '{0}' asks for the new material translator, which UE.DreamPassOutput does not support; remove 'bEnableNewHLSLGenerator' from it.
codes.meaning: A `mesh` pass's override `Material` sets `bEnableNewHLSLGenerator`, and `UE.DreamPassOutput` does not implement the new material translator; the material's own `.dss` reports the same, as DSH5301. Checked on Unreal Engine 5.8 and later, where the Custom Pass runtime is.
codes.fix: Remove `bEnableNewHLSLGenerator` from the material's `#pragma material`.

codes.title: Fullscreen pass '{0}' reads {1} and writes {2} buffers, and the pixel slot a '.usf' pass runs in has {3} inputs and {4} outputs.
codes.meaning: An HLSL pass binds more than its slot holds. A `compute` pass and a `fullscreen` pass with `Shader` run in a fixed shader slot -- the pixel slot for a fullscreen `.usf`, whatever its output count -- with 8 inputs (`DP_Input0` to `DP_Input7`) and 4 outputs.
codes.fix: Split the pass in two, or pack values into fewer buffers (an `RGBA16F` buffer holds four channels).

codes.title: '{0}' is a {1}, and the parameter block of a shader slot holds numbers only, so no texture parameter reaches a '.usf' pass. A material takes one through 'param': draw this pass with a material ('Material = ...'), or let a fullscreen material pass that takes the texture by 'param' write it into a buffer this pass reads.
codes.fix: A texture parameter reaches a material through `param`, never a slot: draw the pass with `Material = ...` and hand the material the texture with `param`, or let a fullscreen material pass take it by `param` and write it into a buffer the `.usf` pass then `read`s. For too many numbers, pass fewer, or pack them into `float4` uniforms yourself.

codes.title: Pass '{0}' writes scene colour, which is {1} at {2}, and '{3}' with it, which is {4}; targets drawn together have one size.
codes.meaning: A `fullscreen` pass with `Shader` and several outputs writes `SceneColor` together with a buffer of another size, and targets drawn together have one size. The scene colour is at scale 1: render resolution before the upscaler, output resolution from `PostProcess.ReplaceTonemapper` on. A `mesh` pass is not checked here: it may not write a buffer of the pipeline beside a texture of the scene at all (DSH7343).
codes.fix: Give the buffer the scene colour's size at that point: `Scale = 1` (the default) and the matching `Resolution`, which a buffer takes from its first writer when it does not say. Write a buffer of another size in a pass of its own.

codes.title: Pass '{0}' replaces the tonemapper, and so does '{1}'; one view runs one tonemapper, so a pipeline replaces it at most once.
codes.meaning: Two messages, both about `PostProcess.ReplaceTonemapper`: a second pass of the pipeline runs there, and one view runs one tonemapper; or the pass that runs there writes no `SceneColor`, and the tonemapper's replacement has to make the frame's final colour.
codes.fix: Keep one pass at `PostProcess.ReplaceTonemapper`, with `write SceneColor;`. Work that follows the tonemapper goes to `PostProcess.AfterTonemap`.

codes.title: A 'param' is a parameter of the pipeline (times a number, plus a number), 'DreamPassWeight' (the same), or a value the compiler can fold, and this is none of them.
codes.meaning: A `param` value cannot be stored in the pipeline asset, which holds a constant, or a parameter of the pipeline (or `DreamPassWeight`) times a number plus a number: the value is computed on the CPU once per view, not in the shader. Two messages: an expression of constants the compiler cannot fold; or one over a parameter in another shape -- `Radius * Gust` (two parameters), `1.0 / Radius`, `sin(Radius)`, `Radius > 2 ? 1 : 0`.
codes.fix:
Write `Source * a + b`, with `a` and `b` numbers the compiler can fold, and compute anything else in the shader or the material from the plain parameter:

```hlsl
param Radius = OutlineWidth * 2 + 1;
```

codes.title: What scales or offsets a parameter in a 'param' is one number the compiler can fold; a vector, or a value known only at run time, has no place in the asset's 'Source * a + b'.
codes.meaning: A `param` scales or offsets a parameter by something the asset cannot store. Two messages: the factor or the offset is not one number the compiler can fold -- a vector, as in `OutlineColor * float4(1, 1, 1, 0.5)`, or an expression it cannot evaluate; or the parameter is a `bool` or a `Texture2D`, which is passed on as it is and cannot be scaled.
codes.fix: Scale by one number -- `param Color = OutlineColor * 0.5;` -- and do per-component work in the shader or the material. Pass a `bool` or a texture unchanged.

codes.title: Buffer '{0}' is exported and last written at {1}: opaque and translucent materials that sample it see the previous frame's contents, UI sees this frame's.
codes.meaning: An exported buffer's last writer runs at `AfterBasePass` or later, so its render target is updated after some materials that sample it have drawn. Last written at `AfterBasePass` or `AfterOpaque`: opaque materials see last frame's contents, while translucent and post-process materials and UI see this frame's. Last written at `BeforePostProcess` or later: opaque and translucent materials see last frame's, UI this frame's.
codes.fix: Nothing to fix if a frame of delay is acceptable. To have every reader see this frame's contents, write the buffer at `BeginView` or `BeforeBasePass` -- a `compute` pass, or a `mesh` pass at `BeforeBasePass` with `Depth = None` or `Depth = Own(...)`.

codes.title: Buffer '{0}' is exported, and an exported buffer becomes a render target asset that materials sample, which a '{1}' buffer cannot be; export a float format.
codes.meaning: A buffer is exported in a format that cannot be a sampled render target: `Depth32`, or an integer format. An exported buffer becomes a render target asset that materials, UMG and Niagara sample as a float texture.
codes.fix: Export a float or normalized format. For depth, have a pass write it into an `R32F` buffer and export that; a mesh pass can write `UE.PixelDepth()` through `UE.DreamPassOutput`.

codes.title: No pass writes buffer '{0}', so whoever reads it reads its 'Clear' value.
codes.meaning: No pass writes the buffer -- no `write`, and no mesh pass's `Depth = Own(...)` -- so every read of it gets its `Clear` value. Usually a writer was renamed or removed.
codes.fix: Write it in a pass, or remove it and its readers. A value that is the same everywhere reaches a pass as a `param`, not as a buffer.

codes.title: No pass reads buffer '{0}' and it is not exported, so writing it is wasted work; read it, export it, or remove it.
codes.meaning: A pass writes the buffer and nothing reads it -- no `read` of it or of its `.Previous`, no mesh pass's `Depth = Own(...)` -- and it is not exported, so writing it is wasted GPU work.
codes.fix: Read it in a later pass, export it (`Export = true`) for materials to sample, or remove it and its writes.

codes.title: 'Mode = Own' draws every primitive with its own material, so the 'Material' of mesh pass '{0}' is never used.
codes.fix: Remove what is unused, or switch the mesh pass to `Mode = Override` (everything drawn with the `Material`) or `Mode = OwnOrOverride` (the primitive's own material where it has `UE.DreamPassOutput`, the override elsewhere).

codes.title: The materials, shader files and pass layers this pipeline names are not available here, so they were taken as written and the checks that need them were skipped; compile the pipeline in the editor to have them checked.
codes.meaning:
Some checks of the pipeline were skipped. Two messages:

- The pipeline was bound by a tool that runs without the editor, so the materials, `.usf` files and pass layers it names are taken as written: whether a material exists and what it offers a pass, whether a shader file and its `Entry` exist, and whether a layer is in the project settings are not checked.
- The engine is older than Unreal Engine 5.8 and has no Custom Pass runtime: what a material offers a pass -- its `UserSceneTexture` inputs, its `UE.DreamPassOutput` pins, its usage flags, its pre-exposure and translator settings -- is not read or checked, and the pipeline is not built on this engine.
codes.fix: Nothing to fix. Compile the pipeline in the editor, on 5.8 or later, to have every reference checked.

codes.title: Pass '{0}' holds a second 'hlsl' block, and the code of a pass is one block; the one on line {1} is it.
codes.meaning: A pass holds two `hlsl` blocks. The code of a pass is one block: whole functions, or the statements of its entry.
codes.fix: Merge them into one block. Functions two passes share go in the file's `hlsl` block.

codes.title: This file already has an 'hlsl' block, on line {0}, and a '.dsp' has one: write every shared function and entry in it.
codes.meaning: The file has a second `hlsl` block at file scope. A `.dsp` has one: the code every pass whose HLSL is in the file is compiled with, and the entries passes pick with `Entry = X;`.
codes.fix: Move the second block's text into the first.

codes.title: Pass '{0}' runs the shader file '{1}' and holds an 'hlsl' block as well, and the code of a pass is in one place: remove 'Shader' to run the block, or the block to run the file.
codes.meaning: A pass names a shader file (`Shader = "..."`) and holds an `hlsl` block as well. The code of a pass is in one place.
codes.fix: Remove `Shader` -- and `Entry`, unless it names a function of the block -- to run the block, or remove the block to run the file.

codes.title: The 'hlsl' block of pass '{0}' holds the statements of its entry, whose function the compiler writes, so 'Entry' has no function to name; remove it, or write whole functions in the block: '{1}'.
codes.meaning: The pass's `hlsl` block holds statements only -- no function definition, `groupshared`, `struct`, `cbuffer` or `[numthreads(...)]` at its top level -- so it is the statements of an entry whose function the compiler writes, and `Entry` has no function to name.
codes.fix: Remove `Entry`, or write the whole function in the block (`[numthreads(8, 8, 1)] void Main(uint3 Id : SV_DispatchThreadID) { ... }` for a compute pass). With whole functions `Entry` names one of them, and is `Main` when it is not written.

codes.title: '#include' cannot stand among the statements of a function, and the 'hlsl' block of pass '{0}' holds the statements of its entry; include the file in the file's 'hlsl' block, or write whole functions in the pass's block.
codes.meaning: A block that holds the statements of an entry has an `#include` among them. The compiler writes those statements inside a function, where HLSL allows no include.
codes.fix: Include the file in the file's `hlsl` block, whose code every pass with HLSL in the `.dsp` is compiled with, or write whole functions in the pass's block and include the file at its top.

codes.title: '{0}' is a name of pass '{1}', and its 'hlsl' block holds the statements of a function the compiler writes, which names its own values {2}; rename the binding.
codes.meaning: A pass whose block holds the statements of its entry binds a name the function the compiler writes gives its own values: `Id`, `GroupId`, `LocalId` and `LocalIndex` in a compute pass; `SvPosition`, `Pixel` and `UV` in a fullscreen one. Every binding is a `#define` of the pass's slot, and would replace that parameter or local.
codes.fix: Rename the binding (`read Scene = SceneColor;` rather than `read UV = SceneColor;`), or write whole functions in the block, which name their parameters themselves.

codes.title: '{0}' is in the shared code of the file's 'hlsl' block, and is the entry of pass '{1}' as well, which the pass's slot renames to the slot's entry point with a #define; the shared code is compiled into that slot, after it. Rename it in the block.
codes.meaning: A name in the shared code of the file's `hlsl` block -- everything in it that no pass names with `Entry` -- is also one the slot of a pass whose HLSL is in the `.dsp` defines: a `read`, `write` or `param` name, its `Size` or `UVRect` name, or the pass's entry, which its slot renames to the slot's entry point. The shared code is compiled into the slot of every such pass after those `#define`s, so the name would be replaced there -- also as a parameter or a local variable of a helper.
codes.fix: Rename it in the block: a helper's parameter `Spread`, not the pass's `SigmaTexels`. Code that uses a pass's names belongs in an entry, which is compiled only into the slots of the passes that name it.

codes.title: '{0}' is the entry of pass '{1}' in the file's 'hlsl' block, and is called here; an entry is compiled only into the slots of the passes that name it, so nothing else can call it. Move what it shares into a function of its own in the block, and call that.
codes.meaning: An entry of the file's `hlsl` block -- a function a pass names with `Entry = X;` alone -- is called: from the shared code, from another entry, or from a pass's own block. In the slot of every pass that does not name it, the entry is blanked out of the shared code, so the call would not compile there.
codes.fix: Move what the entry and its caller share into a function of its own in the block, and call that from both.

codes.title: A {0} pass runs no HLSL of its own, so pass '{1}' cannot hold an 'hlsl' block.
codes.meaning: An `hlsl` block in a pass that runs no HLSL of its own: a fullscreen pass that draws a `Material`, or a `mesh`, `clear` or `copy` pass.
codes.fix: Remove the block. A fullscreen pass runs HLSL when it has no `Material`: remove that instead to run the block.

codes.title: %s contains an invalid folder segment.
codes.meaning: The asset name a source declares contains a folder segment that cannot be part of a package path: empty (`A//B`), `.` or `..`, or a character the engine refuses in a path.
codes.fix: Write the name as plain folders and an asset name: `Characters/Hero/M_Hero`.

codes.title: DreamShader Root '%s' references project plugin '%s', but no enabled plugin with that name was found.
codes.meaning: A source says where its asset goes with a root: `Game`, `Engine`, or `Plugin.<Name>` (in 1.x `Root = "..."` on the block; in 2.0 the source root the file lies under, or `/// @name` with an object path). This root names a plugin no enabled plugin of the project answers to.
codes.fix: Check the plugin's name (the `.uplugin` file name, not its friendly name) and that it is enabled for this project.

codes.title: DreamShader Root '%s' must reference a project plugin under '%s'.
codes.meaning: A source says where its asset goes with a root: `Game`, `Engine`, or `Plugin.<Name>` (in 1.x `Root = "..."` on the block; in 2.0 the source root the file lies under, or `/// @name` with an object path). This root names a plugin that is not one of the project's own (an engine or marketplace plugin). DreamShader only writes assets into plugins under the project's `Plugins` folder.
codes.fix:
Target a project plugin, or `Game`.

A cook does not abort over such a source: the assets it describes are the plugin's own, and no host project can generate into that mount or even edit the file. The failure is logged as `[Cook] Not this project's to build (plugin '<Name>')` and the cook goes on — the plugin ships those assets, and they are what gets packaged. See [Cook behaviour](../generation/ephemeral.md#cook-behaviour).

codes.title: DreamShader Root '%s' references project plugin '%s', but the plugin is not enabled.
codes.meaning: A source says where its asset goes with a root: `Game`, `Engine`, or `Plugin.<Name>` (in 1.x `Root = "..."` on the block; in 2.0 the source root the file lies under, or `/// @name` with an object path). The plugin exists and is disabled, so its content path is not mounted.
codes.fix: Enable the plugin in the `.uproject` or the Plugins window.

codes.title: DreamShader Root '%s' references project plugin '%s', but the plugin cannot contain content.
codes.meaning: A source says where its asset goes with a root: `Game`, `Engine`, or `Plugin.<Name>` (in 1.x `Root = "..."` on the block; in 2.0 the source root the file lies under, or `/// @name` with an object path). The plugin is enabled and its descriptor says `CanContainContent: false`.
codes.fix: Set `"CanContainContent": true` in the `.uplugin`.

codes.title: DreamShader Root '%s' references project plugin '%s', but its Content directory does not exist: '%s'.
codes.meaning: A source says where its asset goes with a root: `Game`, `Engine`, or `Plugin.<Name>` (in 1.x `Root = "..."` on the block; in 2.0 the source root the file lies under, or `/// @name` with an object path). The plugin can hold content, and its `Content` directory is not on disk.
codes.fix: Create the folder the message names.

codes.title: DreamShader Root '%s' references project plugin '%s', but the plugin content is not mounted.
codes.meaning: A source says where its asset goes with a root: `Game`, `Engine`, or `Plugin.<Name>` (in 1.x `Root = "..."` on the block; in 2.0 the source root the file lies under, or `/// @name` with an object path). The plugin's content directory exists and the engine has not mounted it -- typically a plugin that was enabled or created while the editor was running.
codes.fix: Restart the editor (or the commandlet run) so the mount point is registered.

codes.title: DreamShader Root '%s' has an invalid plugin name.
codes.meaning: A source says where its asset goes with a root: `Game`, `Engine`, or `Plugin.<Name>` (in 1.x `Root = "..."` on the block; in 2.0 the source root the file lies under, or `/// @name` with an object path). The plugin part of this root is empty or not a name (`Plugin.` with nothing after it).
codes.fix: Write `Plugin.MyPlugin`.

codes.title: DreamShader Root '%s' has an invalid plugin name.
codes.meaning: Same as DSH8095, for the `Plugins.<Name>` spelling of the root.
codes.fix: Write `Plugins.MyPlugin`.

codes.title: DreamShader Root '%s' has an invalid package root.
codes.meaning: A source says where its asset goes with a root: `Game`, `Engine`, or `Plugin.<Name>` (in 1.x `Root = "..."` on the block; in 2.0 the source root the file lies under, or `/// @name` with an object path). This root is none of those, or resolves to a package root the engine does not know.
codes.fix: Use `Game`, `Engine` or `Plugin.<Name>`.

codes.title: DreamShader asset name must resolve to a non-empty asset path.
codes.meaning: The declared asset name is empty once trimmed.
codes.fix: Give the block a `Name`, or the export a name.

codes.title: DreamShader asset name must resolve to a non-empty asset path.
codes.meaning: The declared asset name consists of separators only (`/`), so no asset name is left.
codes.fix: End the path in an asset name: `Folder/M_Example`.

codes.title: DreamShader asset name '%s' produced an invalid asset name.
codes.meaning: The last segment of the declared asset name is not a valid object name (it contains a character such as `.`, `:` or a space the engine refuses).
codes.fix: Rename the asset using letters, digits and `_`.

codes.title: Asset '%s' is open in an asset editor, so it was NOT rebuilt. An open editor works on its own copy of the asset and writes that copy back when you press Apply or Save,
codes.meaning: The asset is open in an asset editor. An open editor works on a copy of the asset and writes it back on Apply or Save, which would undo the rebuild; a material editor with unsaved changes may also have diverged from the source.
codes.fix: Close that asset's editor tab and compile again.

codes.title: Asset '%s' already exists and is not a Material.
codes.meaning: A package already sits where the material would go, and the object in it is not a UMaterial.
codes.fix: Rename the source's product, or move the existing asset.

codes.title: Asset '%s' already exists and was not generated by DreamShader. Rename your shader or move/delete the existing asset before regenerating.
codes.meaning: A material already sits at the target path and carries no DreamShader provenance, so it was made by hand. DreamShader never overwrites an asset it did not generate.
codes.fix: Rename the product, move or delete the hand-made asset, or decompile it into a source first.

codes.title: Failed to create package '%s'.
codes.meaning: `CreatePackage` failed for the material's package -- an invalid long package name, or the engine refusing the mount point.
codes.fix: Check the root and folder of the product; the log line above it has the engine's reason.

codes.title: Failed to create material '%s'.
codes.meaning: The UMaterial object could not be created in its package.
codes.fix: Look for an engine error right above it in the log (a name clash with a redirector is the usual cause); fix up redirectors in that folder.

codes.title: Asset '%s' already exists and is not a DreamShader instance material. Delete it (or remove Backend="Instance") before switching backends.
codes.meaning: `Backend = ThinCustom` builds a DreamShader instance material, and the asset at that path is of another class (a plain material from an earlier Graph build, usually).
codes.fix: Delete the old asset, or keep the backend it was built with.

codes.title: Asset '%s' already exists and was not generated by DreamShader. Rename your shader or move/delete the existing asset before regenerating.
codes.meaning: Same as DSH8103, for a ThinCustom instance: the existing asset was not generated by DreamShader.
codes.fix: Rename the product, or move or delete the existing asset.

codes.title: Failed to create package '%s'.
codes.meaning: `CreatePackage` failed for a ThinCustom instance's package.
codes.fix: Check the product's root and folder.

codes.title: Failed to create instance material '%s'.
codes.meaning: The ThinCustom instance material object could not be created.
codes.fix: Look for the engine's error above it in the log.

codes.title: Asset '%s' already exists as '%s', but %s generation requires '%s'. Delete or move the existing asset and regenerate it.
codes.meaning: A function asset exists at the target path with another class than the source builds: a plain MaterialFunction where the source is a layer, a layer where it is a blend. The three are distinct engine classes and an asset cannot change class in place.
codes.fix: Delete or move the existing asset and compile again; references to it have to be re-made, so prefer a new name when the old asset is in use.

codes.title: Asset '%s' already exists and is not a MaterialFunction asset.
codes.meaning: A package already sits where the function would go, and the object in it is no material function at all.
codes.fix: Rename the product, or move the existing asset.

codes.title: Asset '%s' already exists and was not generated by DreamShader. Rename your function or move/delete the existing asset before regenerating.
codes.meaning: A material function already sits at the target path and was not generated by DreamShader.
codes.fix: Rename the function, move or delete the existing asset, or decompile it into a source first.

codes.title: Failed to create package '%s'.
codes.meaning: `CreatePackage` failed for a function's package.
codes.fix: Check the product's root and folder.

codes.title: Failed to create material function '%s'.
codes.meaning: The material function object could not be created.
codes.fix: Look for the engine's error above it in the log.

codes.title: Asset '%s' was edited by hand since DreamShader generated it from '%s', so it was NOT rebuilt (rebuilding would destroy those edits). %s
codes.meaning: the asset no longer matches the output digest stamped at its last generation -- somebody edited it by hand, and a rebuild would destroy that work
codes.fix:
answer the notification, or right-click the asset > DreamShader: **Revert to Source** (the source was right), **Adopt Into Source** (the asset was right), **Detach From DreamShader** (neither, stop managing it). `-Force` does not get past this

**See** [Divergence](../generation/divergence.md)

codes.title: Generated DreamShader asset '%s' could not be saved.
codes.meaning: A generated asset could not be written to disk: the `.uasset` is read-only or checked in, another process holds it, or the disk is full.
codes.fix: Check the file out / clear the read-only flag and compile again. Until then the asset exists in memory only.

codes.title: Generated DreamShader asset packages could not be saved.%s
codes.meaning: Saving the batch of generated packages failed; the list after the message names each package and why.
codes.fix: Fix the first cause listed (usually a read-only file) and compile again.

codes.title: Asset Path root '%s' references plugin '%s', but no enabled plugin with that name was found.
codes.meaning: `Path(Root, "Folder/Asset")` resolves its first argument to a mount point: `Game`, `Engine`, or `Plugin.<Name>` / `Plugins.<Name>`. This one names a plugin that no enabled plugin answers to.
codes.fix: Check the plugin's name and that it is enabled.

codes.title: Asset Path root '%s' references plugin '%s', but the plugin is not enabled.
codes.meaning: `Path(Root, "Folder/Asset")` resolves its first argument to a mount point: `Game`, `Engine`, or `Plugin.<Name>` / `Plugins.<Name>`. The plugin exists and is disabled.
codes.fix: Enable it.

codes.title: Asset Path root '%s' references plugin '%s', but the plugin cannot contain content.
codes.meaning: `Path(Root, "Folder/Asset")` resolves its first argument to a mount point: `Game`, `Engine`, or `Plugin.<Name>` / `Plugins.<Name>`. The plugin cannot contain content (`CanContainContent: false`).
codes.fix: Point the reference at a plugin that holds the asset, or enable content in the `.uplugin`.

codes.title: Asset Path root '%s' references plugin '%s', but its Content directory does not exist: '%s'.
codes.meaning: `Path(Root, "Folder/Asset")` resolves its first argument to a mount point: `Game`, `Engine`, or `Plugin.<Name>` / `Plugins.<Name>`. The plugin's `Content` directory is missing on disk.
codes.fix: Check the path the message prints.

codes.title: Asset Path root '%s' references plugin '%s', but the plugin content is not mounted.
codes.meaning: `Path(Root, "Folder/Asset")` resolves its first argument to a mount point: `Game`, `Engine`, or `Plugin.<Name>` / `Plugins.<Name>`. The plugin's content is not mounted in this session.
codes.fix: Restart the editor so the plugin's mount point is registered.

codes.title: Relative asset Path(...) references require a root such as Game, Engine, or Plugin.PluginName.
codes.meaning: `Path("Folder/Asset")` with one argument has to be an absolute object path (`/Game/...`). A relative path needs the root as its first argument.
codes.fix: Write `Path(Game, "Folder/Asset")`.

codes.title: Asset Path root '%s' has an invalid plugin name.
codes.meaning: The plugin part of a `Plugin.<Name>` or `Plugins.<Name>` root is empty or not a name.
codes.fix: Write `Path(Plugin.MyPlugin, "Folder/Asset")`.

codes.title: Asset Path root '%s' has an invalid plugin name.
codes.meaning: Same as DSH8124, for the slash spellings `Plugin/<Name>` and `Plugins/<Name>`.
codes.fix: Write `Path(Plugin.MyPlugin, "Folder/Asset")`.

codes.title: Unsupported asset Path root '%s'. Use Game, Engine, or Plugin.PluginName.
codes.meaning: The first argument of `Path(...)` is none of the roots DreamShader knows.
codes.fix: Use `Game`, `Engine`, or `Plugin.<Name>`.

codes.title: Asset reference cannot be empty.
codes.meaning: An asset reference is empty: `Path()`, an empty string, or a default left blank.
codes.fix: Name the asset, or remove the reference.

codes.title: Asset Path(...) reference is missing a closing ')'.
codes.meaning: `Path(` is never closed.
codes.fix: Add the `)`.

codes.title: Asset Path(...) contains an unterminated string literal.
codes.meaning: A string inside `Path(...)` has no closing quote.
codes.fix: Close the string.

codes.title: Asset Path(...) expects either 1 argument (/Game/... path) or 2 arguments (Game|Engine|Plugin.PluginName, asset path).
codes.meaning: `Path(...)` has no argument or more than two.
codes.fix: Write `Path("/Game/Folder/Asset")` or `Path(Game, "Folder/Asset")`.

codes.title: Asset reference requires a non-empty path.
codes.meaning: The path part of an asset reference is empty (`Path(Game, "")`).
codes.fix: Write the asset's folder and name.

codes.title: Invalid asset path '%s'.
codes.meaning: What the reference resolves to is not a valid object path: it has a character the engine refuses, a doubled `/`, or no asset name.
codes.fix: Copy the reference from the Content Browser (*Copy Reference*).

codes.title: DSH8133: '{0}' is built from '{1}', a file of an installed package, which the package's installer replaces on every update; anything adopted into it would be lost then. Use Revert to Source to undo the edit, or Detach to keep the asset as it is.
codes.meaning: *Adopt Into Source* (or *Adopt Tweaks Into Source*) was asked of an asset a package builds. The package's files belong to its installer, which replaces them on every update, so whatever Adopt wrote into them would be lost with the next one -- and with it the edit it was meant to keep. Nothing was written.
codes.fix: Use *Revert to Source* to throw the hand edit away, or *Detach* to keep the asset as it is and stop generating it. To change what the package builds, change the package (upstream, or a copy of it outside `Packages`).

codes.title: DSH8149: '{0}' uses conditional compilation, and '{1}' holds only the branch that was taken -- adopting it would write that one branch back over the file and delete the rest. Move the change into the matching branch of the source by hand, or use DreamShader > Detach first if this asset should stop being generated from it.
codes.meaning: **Adopt Into Source** was asked to rewrite a source that uses conditional compilation (`#if` / `#ifdef` / `#ifndef`). Adopt rebuilds the source text from the asset, and the asset only ever holds the branch that was taken -- so adopting would write that one branch back over the file and silently delete every other branch
codes.fix:
move the change into the matching branch of the source by hand (the decompiler's output for the asset is a good starting point), or use **Detach From DreamShader** first if this asset should stop being generated from that source. Revert and Detach are unaffected, since neither writes the source

**See** [Preprocessor](../language/preprocessor.md), [Divergence](../generation/divergence.md)

codes.title: rebuilding '%s' from '%s' dropped %d parameter override(s) the rebuilt material no longer declares: %s.
codes.meaning: a rebuild of a ThinCustom material captured the parameter overrides set on the generated instance and put them back afterwards, but one or more of them named a parameter the rebuilt material no longer declares -- the source renamed it, removed it, or changed its kind -- so those values had nowhere to go and were dropped. Restoration matches by name and kind, because a name is the only thing that survives a graph the generator tears down and rebuilds. The same line reports an override of a parameter kind this build cannot re-apply (a texture collection, for instance)
codes.fix:
nothing is broken and the rebuild succeeded; set the value again on the instance under its new name, or move it into the source as a `Properties` default so no override is needed. If the parameter was renamed and you want the value carried across, rename it back, rebuild, then rename once more in the same edit as the override

**See** [Divergence](../generation/divergence.md#parameter-overrides-on-a-generated-thincustom-instance)

codes.title: '{0}' does not resolve to a valid asset path. {1}
codes.meaning: The product's asset name, or the `/// @name /Game/...` path override, does not resolve to a package path Unreal will accept. The quoted 1.x message says which rule broke: an empty leaf after sanitising, a folder segment that sanitises to nothing, a `Root` naming a plugin that is not enabled or cannot host content, or a path Unreal itself rejects.
codes.fix: Read the quoted message first — it names the offending segment. A `@name` that is a bare leaf replaces only the asset name and keeps the root rules; a `@name` starting with `/` is a full path whose last segment is the asset and whose leading segments are the root, so `/Game/X/M_Y` puts `M_Y` under `/Game/X`. A file under a plugin source root defaults to that plugin's content mount, so it needs no `/Game` prefix at all.

codes.title: The material for '{0}' could not be created or reused. {1}
codes.meaning: The destination for a material product exists and is not a `UMaterial`, or it exists on disk without DreamShader's source metadata, or the package could not be created. The last case is rare and usually means the path is not writable.
codes.fix: For "already exists and was not generated by DreamShader": that guard is the reason a hand-authored material at the same path is never cleared and overwritten. Rename the shader, or move or delete the existing asset, then compile again.

codes.title: The material function for '{0}' could not be created or reused. {1}
codes.meaning: As DSH8201, for a material function product — with one extra way to fail: the asset at that path exists as the wrong function class. A `@layer` needs a `UMaterialFunctionMaterialLayer`, a `@layerblend` needs a `UMaterialFunctionMaterialLayerBlend`, and a plain export needs a `UMaterialFunction`. Changing the kind of an exported function changes the class it must become.
codes.fix: Delete or move the existing asset and regenerate it. The class cannot be changed in place: every material that calls the function holds a typed reference to it.

codes.title: The ThinCustom instance for '{0}' could not be created or reused. {1}
codes.meaning: As DSH8201, for the `UDreamShaderMaterialInstance` a ThinCustom material becomes.
codes.fix: Same as DSH8201. If the asset exists as a plain `UMaterial`, the file used to compile with `Backend = "Graph"` and now asks for ThinCustom (or the project default changed); delete the old material or pin the backend back with `#pragma material(Backend = "Graph")`.

codes.title: The emitter needs the builtin catalog the front end was bound against, but the emit context carries none.
codes.meaning: `EmitDreamShaderIRProduct` was called with no `FIREmitContext::Catalog`, or with an empty one. The catalog is how the emitter turns an attribute name into an `EMaterialProperty` and how it resolves a reflected class precisely, so it cannot proceed without it.
codes.fix: Internal: the pipeline builds the catalog once per run and must pass the SAME one the binder used. If this reaches a user, the catalog manifest failed to load or reflection produced nothing; the reflection filler only logs that case (`BuildBuiltinCatalogFromReflection` runs before any compile and has no sink to raise into, so it has no code).

codes.title: Product index {0} does not exist in this module, which has {1}.
codes.meaning: An internal inconsistency: the product index is out of range for the module, or the graph's topological order names a node the graph does not have.
codes.fix: Not an authoring error. Report it with the source file; `dsc dump-ir` on the same file shows the graph the emitter was handed.

codes.title: '{0}' is open in an asset editor, so it was not rebuilt. {1}
codes.meaning: The asset is open in an asset editor. An open editor does not edit the asset itself: it duplicates it and copies the duplicate back on Apply or Save, so an editor open across a rebuild holds a pre-rebuild copy and the next Apply silently reverts everything the rebuild did.
codes.fix: Close the asset editor and compile again. Refusing is the only safe answer available: whether that copy has unsaved edits is private to the MaterialEditor module, and closing it blindly would pop a save prompt in the middle of a compile-on-save.
